title: The snail and the string

data.source: 300 noisy rotor paths (R4, flat potential), one path that never steps back, and two hand-made loops.

prediction: The cut count equals the number of half-turn rungs passed by the running maximum of the path, always; it equals the half-turns wound only when the path never steps back; a there-and-back loop has winding number 0 but 2 cuts, so the count is not a topological invariant.
baseline: The winding number (degree) of a loop on the circle, and the ladder process of a running maximum (Feller).
why: Every claim held. The count is not the winding number: it is the ladder count of the running maximum, a standard object, and the coherence is the total distance travelled. Topology keeps only the net turns; CRR keeps the high-water mark and the mileage.
